Hi Ryan — great to meet the Skylab team today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can lock the performance gating before the pilot kickoff.

Summary from demo:
- Skylab target: conversational agent for provider support (avg response length ~180 tokens), streaming responses into triage UI.
- Business SLOs discussed: 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 250ms for 128-token final responses, 99th percentile graceful degradation to a cheaper model.
- Throughput/peak: expected peak concurrent sessions ~120 (burst to 200 for short windows).
- Data residency: US-only VPC for pilot.

Open technical questions we flagged:
1) Preferred GPU family: Skylab asked for guidance on H100 vs A100 and a lower-cost L4 option for mixed workloads.
2) Exact streaming latency budget per hop (frontend->inference->frontend) so we can size reserved throughput.
3) Acceptance criteria for pilot: pass a 24h smoke run at 75% peak with <2% token-drop/timeout.

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO fitment matrix and a pilot test plan with bench steps.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik to propose a short GPU sizing matrix (A100/H100/L4) and reserved throughput recommendations by EOD tomorrow.
- Ben to collect a representative traffic trace from Skylab (sample requests + token distribution) — Ryan, can your ops team share that?
- Naomi to circulate mutual action plan and contract touchpoints for Dedicated capacity pilot.

Thanks — Naomi

Thanks Naomi — good session. Quick clarifications from our side:

- On GPU choices: cost is a factor, but we cannot miss the 95p latency target for short responses. If H100 materially drops median/95p latency for streaming, we need to understand the $/token delta.

We can pull a 24-hour traffic sample — procurement@ will coordinate with your Ben. Also: procurement will want a draft of the reserved throughput commitment (tokens/s and concurrency guarantees) and any SLAs for CPU fallback.

Hi Ryan — quick technical notes addressing the GPU/latency/throughput questions. Attaching an abbreviated matrix below; I'll send the full benchmark plan if this aligns.

Short answers:
- Is <80ms first-token feasible on Dedicated? Not for heavy encoder-decoder models at high concurrency unless we use H100 + optimized kernels + continuous batching suppression. For a causal decoder (quantized) on A100, first-token of 80-120ms is realistic at modest concurrency (<=100).

GPU tradeoffs (very high level):
- H100: best 95p latency for streaming and fastest cold-start token RT; higher $/hour. Preferred if 95p < 150ms is a hard requirement for your peak workload.
- A100: strong middle ground for throughput and latency; more cost-efficient at scale. Good if you target 95p < 250ms and can accept slightly higher tail.
- L4 (or similar inference-class): excellent for 1–2 token responses and massive scale at low cost, but long responses and large KV caches blow up latency. Use as overflow or for smaller prompt routes.

Reserved throughput sizing (proposal):
- Baseline: provision for sustained 140 concurrent inference requests (conservative given your 120 active users + 2x per-session).
- Token-rate target: plan reserved capacity for 18,000 tokens/s sustained to cover steady workloads (assumes average 1.5 requests/s * 120 sessions * 100 tokens/request).
- Burst headroom: reserve +50% burst (27,000 tokens/s) for short windows — handled via autoscale + burst slab.

Pilot acceptance criteria (technical):
- 24h smoke run at 75% sustained load (13,500 tokens/s) with 95p E2E latency <= 250ms and <1% error/timeouts.
- Streaming objective: first-byte to client <120ms for 90% of requests and steady-state token emission >= 12ms/token for 90%.

Next steps from engineering:
- If Skylab prioritizes tail latency, we recommend H100 on Reserved pilot. If cost matters more than 95p tail, start on A100 with L4 as a fallback route.
- I'll circulate a microbench harness and ask for a representative trace (Ben owns).

-Karthik

Mutual action plan (pilot window: 4 weeks):
1) Data & traces (Skylab) — due EOD Mon 4/19: anonymized 24-hour trace + token length distribution (Ben to coordinate).
2) Microbench (Redwood) — Karthik to deliver GPU matrix + estimated $/token delta (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and recommended reserved rates by Tue 4/20.
3) Pilot provisioning (Redwood) — create Dedicated pilot pool with A100 baseline + H100 option for tail-sensitive routes; reserved throughput slab: 18k tokens/s sustained + 27k tokens/s burst.
4) Acceptance test (joint) — 24h smoke run at 75% sustained; KPIs: 95p E2E <= 250ms, first-byte <120ms for 90% of requests, <1% timeouts.
5) Contracting/procurement — Naomi to share a draft reserved-capacity term sheet with pricing options and a one-week SLAs appendix for review.

Concrete asks for procurement team:
- Please confirm whether Skylab can accept the proposed reserved throughput slab (18k sustained / 27k burst) or prefers a lower committed baseline with higher overage rates.
- Budget range: if you can share an initial target (monthly committed spend), we can map GPU choices to cost.

Attachments included: slo-fitment-matrix.xlsx (contains the A100/H100/L4 rows with benchmark estimates) and redwood-pilot-test-plan.pdf (bench steps, telemetry hooks, and acceptance checklist).

I'll follow up with the term sheet and a pricing appendix once Karthik's matrix is in. Thanks all — Naomi
